images.after: What separates a legitimate programmatic page from a doorway page
images.title: The name-swap test
images.alt: Decision test: delete the place or product name from two programmatic pages; if you can't tell them apart, it's one page published many times.
images.caption: Second test: would the page still be worth having if search engines didn't exist?

data.question: Delete the place or product name from two pages. Can you tell which is which?

branches.result: Several real data points change per page. Keep going.
You have one page published many times. Fix the data first.

images.after: 3. Design a template where the data does the talking
images.title: A template that adapts to its data
images.alt: Checklist for a programmatic page template: unique data first, short boilerplate, conditional sections, a notes field, unique titles and internal links.
images.caption: A page that adapts to its data reads like it was made for that entry.

items: Unique information first: tables, local details, specific numbers
Shared boilerplate kept short and pushed down the page
Sections drop out when a row has no data for them
A field for a short written note on unusual entries
Its own title, meta description and heading from the data
Links to related entries and a browsable index page

images.after: 7. Prune what doesn't earn its place
images.title: Four fixes for pages that don't earn
images.alt: Four options for programmatic pages that stay unindexed or get no visits: improve the data, merge into a stronger page, add noindex, or delete.
images.caption: A smaller set of useful pages is safer than a large set of marginal ones.

items.title: Improve the data
items.text: Add the missing details the page needs.

items.title: Merge
items.text: Fold it into a stronger page.

items.title: Add noindex
items.text: Put a noindex tag on the page.

items.title: Delete
items.text: Remove it if it stays unindexed or never gets visits.
